cameras._comment: Accuracy audit (2026-08-22): NOT simulated in the sense the other _SIMULATED cameras are (those reuse cam04's footage through a fake homography) -- this points at two REAL, independently-filmed, ground-truth-labeled videos (their own filenames state the real outcome: 'Candidate was found using a mobile phone in the examination hall'). Playlist cycles 01 then 02, then wraps -- exercising the multi-video-playlist feature (CameraConfig.playlist) instead of looping one clip forever. Calibration here is deliberately coarse (one wide seat_20 zone spanning almost the whole frame, not a precise per-seat homography) because no real measured seating chart exists for this specific room -- exactly the honest caveat this project already applies to every illustrative calibration. It's enough to prove the actual point: confirmed object detection on real footage genuinely produces a genuine, well-justified, non-flooding alert.

Recalibrated 2026-08-23 (v2). v1 used positions eyeballed from a single frame description with no pixel measurement, and produced a real 92-second false 'hand_reach_across' (a wrist keypoint persistently resolving to the wrong seat) -- disconnected immediately, root cause investigated. This pass extracted real frames, overlaid a measured pixel grid (cv2, 100px lines with coordinate labels), and read hand/mouse-work-area coordinates directly off the grid at multiple timestamps, not off a mental estimate. Coverage is DELIBERATELY reduced from 6 seats to 3 (seat_d03/d07/d08): desks 04/05/09/10 remain genuinely ambiguous even under careful grid-referenced review in this single wide-angle/fisheye shot -- overlapping desks at different depths, an unlabeled/occluded placard for one, and two desks (09/10) whose visible activity zones overlap heavily. Forcing coordinates for those would repeat exactly the mistake this recalibration exists to fix; 3 confidently-placed seats beats 6 uncertain ones. Coordinates are the desk's real hand/mouse-work area (where a wrist actually operates), not the monitor or placard position, since that's what nearest_seat() actually needs to get right for gesture detection. Identity homography (image_points == plane_points, the full frame) -- same simplification cam_ground_truth uses. Still not a calibrate_tool.py measurement (no physical access to this room), so still illustrative-grade, not survey-grade -- but now grid-measured, not guessed, and the general MAX_PLAUSIBLE_REACH_SECONDS safeguard (behaviour/gestures.py) remains as a backstop regardless.
